question: Does a working classifier or tracked list of lane results exist in omnimarket, the plugin or the controller, and should it be wired or built?

definitions.wiring_state: wired when at least one evidence entry of kind in_repo_caller, external_caller or schedule counts as a runtime caller; entry_point and bus_subscription alone only register a node and never make it wired. An in_repo_caller that names a caller_equivalent counts only when that equivalent is itself wired.
definitions.reported_state: working only for an equivalent that is wired and whose run read shows it classifying; every unwired equivalent is reported not-working.
definitions.verdict: wire: this equivalent covers the need and is used as it is or wired in; build: it does not cover the need, so the part it leaves is named as a build.

equivalents.covers: classifies every lane TERMINAL receipt by the worse of its claimed outcome and its lane result, appends one class row per receipt (the tracked list) and a reading row

wiring_evidence.detail: event_bus.subscribe_topics is empty and runtime_dispatch is external_trigger: true

wiring_gaps: no in-repo caller imports the node outside its own package
no schedule module or timer unit in the node, unlike node_lane_census_effect
no reference to the node or its topics in omnibase_infra, the plugin repository or omniclaude (git grep at origin/HEAD, empty)
equivalents.verdict_basis: It already classifies and writes the tracked list; what is missing is a trigger that runs it. The build left is a scheduled run of its sweep verb, not a new classifier.

run_read.command: python -m omnimarket.nodes.node_lane_result_sweep_effect probe --since 2026-11-09T00:00:00Z (example overlay, ledger copy taken 2026-11-09T12:01:53Z)
run_read.observed: verdict NOT_WORKING; 2402 receipt verdicts: 2368 unclassified-late, 19 clear, 15 pending; the ledger copy holds 3 lane-result-class rows in total, all appended 2026-11-07T16:42:07Z by one manual run

equivalents.covers: decides how one finished remote lane closes from its engine exit code and its LANE_RESULT or TERMINAL line; keeps no list

wiring_evidence.detail: NODE_CLOSE = node_remote_lane_close_compute, asked through the canonical runtime at lane close (git grep at origin/HEAD, line 653)

wiring_gaps: classifies one lane at close and keeps no list, so it cannot hold a lane to a later review
equivalents.verdict_basis: It is the classifier at the lane's own close and already runs for every remote lane; the sweep reads the TERMINAL rows it shapes. Nothing is left to wire here.

run_read.command: final_lane_outcome('LANE_RESULT outcome=blocked\nBLOCKER: x'), final_lane_outcome('LANE_RESULT outcome=partial'), final_lane_outcome('no result line here')

equivalents.covers: normalizes one error event to a class key; the sweep uses it to key each receipt

wiring_evidence.detail: subscribes onex.cmd.omnimarket.error-class-normalize.v1; the only publisher found is node_lane_failure_recovery_effect
imports the normalizer to key each receipt

wiring_gaps: its only in-repo callers are the unwired sweep and node_hook_refusal_row_compute, which has no importer outside its package
it classifies an error by key and does not read a lane result by itself
equivalents.verdict_basis: It is a part of the sweep and becomes wired when the sweep has its trigger; it is not a second classifier to build.

run_read.command: the sweep probe above, which calls the normalizer per receipt
run_read.observed: receipts carry class keys such as lane.remote-lane-runner.template.731127ecb9

equivalents.covers: normalizes guard OOM and retention failures only and submits a recovery contribution
wiring_gaps: no producer of its command topic and no reference to the node in omnibase_infra, the plugin repository or omniclaude
equivalents.verdict_basis: It covers two failure kinds, not lane results in general, so it does not stand in for a classifier or a list.

run_read.command: git -C $OMNI_HOME/<repo> grep -l node_lane_failure_recovery_effect origin/HEAD, for omnibase_infra, the plugin repository and omniclaude
run_read.observed: no file in any of the three repositories

equivalents.covers: decides whether a lane is live, terminated or dropped from CLAIM and TERMINAL times and hook events; it reads no result class

wiring_evidence.detail: line 135 has the session-resume skill ask the node for every open CLAIM with parent=<your lane> (git grep at origin/HEAD)

wiring_gaps: its verdicts are live, terminated or dropped, so a blocked or failed lane reads terminated
equivalents.verdict_basis: It tracks whether a lane is alive, not what its result was; the result class stays with the sweep.

run_read.command: HandlerLaneLiveness().handle(one observation with claimed_at and terminal_at inside a 1 h window)

equivalents.covers: the rolling ledger's TERMINAL rows are the tracked list of lane results as lanes write them; the adapter reads them for the sweep

wiring_evidence.detail: build_row_source reads the ledger file and its archive
every lane ends with a TERMINAL row appended to the ledger; this lane's ledger copy holds 581 of them in the live file

wiring_gaps: the rows carry the lane's claimed outcome; nothing classifies them without the sweep
equivalents.verdict_basis: The list exists and is filled by every lane; it is the input the sweep classifies.

run_read.command: grep -c '| TERMINAL |' on the ledger copy taken 2026-11-09T12:01:53Z
run_read.observed: 581 TERMINAL rows in the live file

conclusion: A classifier and a tracked list of lane results both exist in omnimarket (the sweep and the ledger TERMINAL rows). The sweep is registered but unwired: nothing runs it, one manual run on 2026-11-07 wrote three class rows, and its own probe reads NOT_WORKING. The build left is a scheduled run of the sweep, not a new classifier.
